title: Gluing Local Contexts into Global Meaning: A Sheaf-Theoretic Decomposition of Transformer Representations
abstract: arXiv:2610.17117v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Prior research into interpretability does not test whether a representation stays consistent under paraphrasing. Each pair of paraphrases can be thought of as a local witness that two activations should be the same. From these local witnesses we can build a cellular sheaf on the paraphrase graph. The question of what is consistent under paraphrasing can be answered by the Laplacian $L_\mathcal{F}$ given a frozen model. No training required. Our kernel $H^0$ gives us a content subspace. We show that with only 20 dims the kernel outperforms the subspace that LEACE retains with all dims on held-out CounterFact fact retrieval by $+17.1$\,pp on average across 8 models. By constraining all paraphrases of a fact together we see an additional increase of $+6.5$\,pp. Our spectral complement shows us where the causal influence is concentrated. tldr: 该论文提出一种无需训练的层论方法：在改写图上构建胞腔层并用其拉普拉斯算子的核 $H^0$ 提取内容子空间，仅 20 维即跨 8 个模型在 CounterFact 事实检索上平均超越 LEACE 全维子空间 +17.1 个百分点，且联合约束同一事实的所有改写可再提升 +6.5 个百分点。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces a training-free sheaf-theoretic method that builds a cellular sheaf on the paraphrase graph and uses the kernel $H^0$ of its Laplacian to extract a content subspace—just 20 dimensions outperforming LEACE's full-dimensional subspace by +17.1 pp on CounterFact fact retrieval across 8 models, with an additional +6.5 pp gain from jointly constraining all paraphrases of a fact.
